evals.name: check-reports-overlay-and-routes-reconfig-natively
evals.expected_output: The check action reads the three rendered ${user_config.batch_*} values and reports the effective posture-batch overlay (excluded / promoted / demoted correctors and the net effect, or that the tiers run as declared when all unset). It routes any reconfiguration to /plugin configure discipline@<marketplace> and never edits settings.json or pluginConfigs. It writes no file: check is read-only.
expectations: Reports the effective batch overlay from the userConfig values, read-only
Routes reconfiguration to the native /plugin configure discipline@<marketplace> flow, never hand-editing pluginConfigs
Writes no file and does not run the apply action

evals.name: unexpanded-token-treated-as-unset
evals.expected_output: When an option was never configured and its ${user_config.…} token survives literally (a zero-config or headless install), the check treats it as unset — no overlay from that key — and does not parse the literal placeholder as a corrector name. Both an empty value and a surviving literal placeholder read as unset.
expectations: Treats a surviving literal ${user_config.…} token as unset, not a value
Does not parse the literal placeholder as a corrector name
Treats an empty value and an unexpanded token identically (unset)

evals.name: validates-names-against-installed-correctors
evals.prompt: discipline setup check (batch_exclude = point-dont-copy, notaskill; batch_promote = scrutinize-dont-coast, use-your-skills)
evals.expected_output: The check globs the installed corrector directories and validates each overlaid name. It reports point-dont-copy as a valid exclusion and flags notaskill in batch_exclude as a FAIL (matches no installed corrector), with remediation to fix the value through the plugin configuration prompt. For batch_promote it warns visibly that scrutinize-dont-coast (never) and use-your-skills (core) are not situational and are not promoted. It flags contradictions (a name both excluded and promoted/demoted) and no-op demotes.
expectations: Validates overlay names against the globbed installed correctors
Flags an unknown exclude/demote name as a FAIL with native-reconfiguration remediation
Warns on non-situational batch_promote entries (never/core/unknown) and does not treat them as successful promotes

evals.name: apply-writes-a-new-discipline-yaml
evals.prompt:
/discipline:setup apply lever_scope=non-trivial

[This repository, a git checkout that is not the home directory, has no docs/conventions/discipline.yaml yet.]
evals.expected_output: Runs check first (lever_scope's repository row is INFO: absent), then calls setup-apply.mjs lever_scope=non-trivial, which creates docs/conventions/discipline.yaml holding lever_scope: non-trivial. It re-runs check and reports PASS lever_scope: non-trivial from that report, then runs the tracked-file pair and says the new file is written but untracked and must be committed to reach the team. It writes no other file and does not touch pluginConfigs or settings.json.
expectations: Runs check before writing and reports the repository file as absent (INFO)
Writes docs/conventions/discipline.yaml through setup-apply.mjs with lever_scope=non-trivial
Reports the value from the re-run check, not from the write
Says the file is written but untracked and must be committed
Does not write pluginConfigs, settings.json or any other file

evals.name: apply-shows-the-diff-before-changing-an-existing-file
evals.prompt:
/discipline:setup apply lever_scope=deterministic

[docs/conventions/discipline.yaml already holds `lever_scope: non-trivial` under a comment line naming the owning team.]
evals.expected_output: setup-apply.mjs exits 3 and prints a unified diff changing lever_scope from non-trivial to deterministic without writing. The skill shows that diff and asks whether to write it, and re-runs with --yes only after an explicit yes; until then the file, comment included, is unchanged.
expectations: Shows the diff from lever_scope: non-trivial to lever_scope: deterministic before any write
Asks the operator to confirm the diff
Does not pass --yes or change the file before an explicit yes, and does not read the apply request as that yes

evals.name: check-warns-on-an-invalid-lever-scope
evals.prompt:
/discipline:setup check

[docs/conventions/discipline.yaml holds `lever_scope: always`; the user's lever_scope option is non-trivial.]
evals.expected_output: The lever_scope repository row is a WARN quoting docs/conventions/discipline.yaml, the key lever_scope and the value always, naming deterministic and non-trivial as the allowed values and pointing at apply as the fix. The effective value it reports is the default deterministic, not the user's non-trivial, because the invalid layer is dropped rather than falling through to a lower one. It is not a FAIL, and check writes nothing.
expectations: Reports a WARN that names docs/conventions/discipline.yaml, lever_scope and always
Reports the effective lever_scope as deterministic, not the user's non-trivial value
Does not report a FAIL and writes nothing
